findings.title: isAccessTokenId checks the wrong characters with an inverted condition, so the grant shortcut is never verified
findings.body: The grant shortcut sits at index 4-5 of the encoded context (e.g. 'onrtac' -> 'ac' at 4-5), but this reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is 'ta' for that example. The check is also inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the case where the grant matches and accepts the case where it does not. Since index 3-4 can never equal a two-letter grant shortcut in practice, the grant check is effectively a no-op. The expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions therefore only verify the 'x:UUID' shape and would accept a token minted with the wrong grant. Fixing only the negation would make every correct token fail, so both the offset and the condition need correcting.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId
findings.body: The third `Objects.requireNonNull` call tests `grantType` again, and its message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. The actual `rawTokenId` parameter is never validated, so a null raw token id is accepted silently and would later produce a token ID such as 'onrtac:null' via encodeTokenId. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: Javadoc asks for a 3-letter grant shortcut, but the encoder requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters'. The encoder (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId) requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 characters and slices the grant shortcut as two fixed characters. A grant factory that follows this doc and returns a 3-letter shortcut gets encoded into a 7-character context, and every token carrying it then fails to decode with IllegalArgumentException. The doc should state the 2-character requirement.

findings.title: Grant shortcut is not validated for length, non-null, or character set
findings.body: postInit takes `gtf.getShortcut()` and uses it directly as a map key. Nothing checks that it is two characters long, which the decoder depends on (length 6 check and fixed 2-char slices in getTokenContextFromTokenId), nor that it is non-null or free of ':'. A null shortcut makes ConcurrentHashMap.put throw NPE and aborts server startup. A shortcut of the wrong length is accepted silently at startup but yields token IDs that cannot be decoded. The only check is the duplicate-size comparison at line 82.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() on a public SPI interface breaks existing implementations
findings.body: `String getShortcut();` is added as an abstract method with no default. Any existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation outside the files updated in this PR (third-party extensions or any in-tree factory not listed) will fail to compile. Even compiled implementations that return null will crash server startup (see the ConcurrentHashMap NPE in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory). A default implementation or a clear upgrade note would avoid this.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes only because of an NPE, not the intended validation
findings.body: The test never calls postInit, so `sessionFactory` is null. The shortcut 'ac' is not in the test's map, so getGrantTypeByShortcut dereferences the null sessionFactory and throws NullPointerException. The test catches any RuntimeException and passes. It therefore does not exercise the intended 'unknown grant shortcut' path (IllegalArgumentException) and would pass even if validation were broken. It should assert the specific exception type and stub the lookup so the failure path is actually tested.

findings.title: Only standard token exchange records the grant type; legacy token exchange tokens fall back to 'na'
findings.body: The grant type is set on the client session context only in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient. TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory is still registered under the legacy TOKEN_EXCHANGE feature with shortcut 'te', and this diff does not touch the legacy exchange path. Access tokens issued through the legacy path therefore get the 'na' fallback in the token ID, so the grant information this PR is meant to provide is missing for that flow. The legacy provider should set Constants.GRANT_TYPE as well, or the gap should be documented.
